ca_freak_brothers_dome.blurb: Freak Brothers Dome is a three-summited formation in the southern Wonderland of Rocks, on the east side of Wonderland Valley in Joshua Tree National Park. It holds eight trad routes ranging from about 5.6 to 5.11, with most falling between 5.8 and 5.10. The character is friction climbing, including some high-angle slab lines. The dome sits across the valley from the big Astro Domes faces. Reaching it means a walk of roughly 600 yards up the Wonderland Valley wash from the backcountry dirt lot.

ca_little_europe.blurb: Little Europe is a small crag beside Geology Tour Road in the Virgin Islands Area of Joshua Tree's Queen Valley. Its eight bolted sport routes suit a short session: one is an easy 5.5, another is 5.8, five are 5.10, and one is 5.11. Because the rocks stand just across the road from a small pullout, the walk is only a few steps. Climbs are found on more than one side of the formation, so a party can choose between sunnier and shadier lines depending on the hour.

ca_jackass_rock.blurb: Jackass Rock is a broken dome of roughly 400 feet along Minarets Road in the Mammoth Pool country of the western Sierra Nevada, more than an hour's drive from either North Fork or Bass Lake. The rock is granodiorite. There are eight problems and routes: five trad lines from 5.8 to the low 5.11s, one sport route at 5.12, and two easy boulder problems. Jackass Creek nearby has swimming holes and a tall waterfall, and the surrounding dome country was heavily burned in the 2020 Creek Fire.

ca_hat_creek_cattle_company.blurb: Hat Creek Cattle Company is a small group of sandstone boulders in a creek bed above Rattlesnake Canyon, in the hills behind Santa Barbara. Oak trees shade the stones and the landings are flat. There are eight problems, mostly around V3, with a spread from V1 up to a couple of much harder lines in the V8 to V9 range. The boulders are tucked away from the main trail, so expect a hike of roughly 35 to 45 minutes, most of it on trail with a final stretch up the stream bed. Poison oak grows nearby.

ca_kelly_s_hill.blurb: Kelly's Hill is one section of the sandstone boulders at The Lizard's Mouth, in the mountains above Santa Barbara. It holds eight problems, from V0 up to about V5, with three of them at V3. From the warm-up boulder at the second pullout, a short climb up the slope to the right leads to a prominent arete that marks the area. The parent area offers a cave traverse and well over a hundred problems, so this hillside is easy to combine with the rest of the Mouth.
